main_body: Flat snow ground patch (4x3 tiles) with tiled pattern of grey-green dark clumps on pale blue-white snow; a terrain surface with no standing volume
top_band: none - flat ground texture, no standing object
evidence: The candidate is a ground terrain tile seen from above, as a ground patch should be. It has no standing body, so the top/front structure rules do not apply. No side faces, no front elevation, no fake object volume. It passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The snow has about 5 lightness steps (white, pale blue-white, light blue-grey, grey-green mid, dark green-grey) plus a few bright white sparkle pixels. The dark clump areas are speckled with several tones, so they are not flat fills. The pale snow areas are large, mostly one flat tone with only sparse blue-shadow pixels, and the repeating blob pattern is very regular, so it looks tiled and mechanical. Tiles carry roughly 6-9 colours, a bit under the reference grass and paving. Overall it is acceptable next to the reference but slightly thinner, with no outlines to judge.
